name: Amansara
positioning: Aman hotel in Siem Reap, in a restored 1960s building that began as a guesthouse for King Norodom Sihanouk's guests
best_for: Travelers who want a base at the doorstep of the Angkor Complex
Guests interested in history and mid-century modernist design

facts.text: The guesthouse hosted Jacqueline Onassis and Josip Broz Tito.
The architect Kerry Hill restored the property, and it reopened as Amansara in 2002.
Hill played up the modernist look with cream walls, green lawns and long corridors.
Suites have timber finishes and terrazzo flooring, with sliding doors and large windows for open-plan living.
The hotel is at the doorstep of the Angkor Complex, which includes the UNESCO World Heritage Site Angkor Wat.
The Royal Garden is within walking distance.
The Kampot Pepper set offers a sampler of Khmer dishes showcasing Cambodian Kampot pepper.
Guests can choose international or local dishes, or both.
The spa building is tucked away from the main courtyard buildings that house the suites.
The spa offers traditional Khmer treatments and a signature Aman massage.

highlights.text: Amansara was first a guesthouse for the guests of King Norodom Sihanouk, known then as Villa Princiére.
Pool suites have a plunge pool in addition to a courtyard.
Guests can join private tours with the hotel's archaeologist, Seng Kompheak.
Guests arrive on one of two black 1960s Mercedes-Benz limousines after fast-track immigration arranged by the hotel.
The hotel can arrange a meditation class with an English-speaking Khmer monk at a local temple.

considerations.text: The hotel sits on a busy arterial road.
Siem Reap Angkor International Airport is a 60-minute drive from the hotel.
The hotel is single-storied, with about two to three steps to negotiate in places.

sources.title: Amansara, Siem Reap, Cambodia - Hotel Review, Condé Nast Traveler
